text:
ellie_c: Customer on prod-us is seeing intermittent 502/504s since ~2026-03-16 14:12 UTC. Can we get a quick repro pack to escalate?

sam_eng: First ask for a single successful and a failing request — we only need minimal bits:
- exact request timestamp (UTC) and timezone
- the full request body (copy-paste) and headers
- response status and the full response body
- response headers (we need any x-request-id / x-trace-id present)
- a HAR or curl that reproduces it

kevin_support: Quick curl to run and attach response headers (makes it easiest for us):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <KEY>\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-1\",\"input\":\"hello\"}'
# Capture headers: add -D - or --dump-header hdr.txt
```

sam_eng: If they can't run curl, ask for a browser HAR: Chrome DevTools > Network > right-click the request > Save as HAR with content. HAR + request body + timestamps is ideal.

kevin_support: For SDKs, tell them to paste any `requestId`/`traceId` from their client logs. Examples:
- Node: `response.headers['x-request-id']`
- Python (requests): `resp.headers.get('x-request-id')`
- Go: `resp.Header.Get("X-Request-Id")`

mobile-dev-bot: Mobile tips: Android `adb logcat | grep -i request` — look for `request_id` or `x-request-id`. iOS: check device console for `x-request-id` or `redwood-trace`. Also include app version and SDK version.

sam_eng: Also ask for: exact region they hit (prod-us/prod-eu), caller IP (if available), and whether they're behind a corporate proxy or CDN. That helps us correlate load balancer vs server errors.

kevin_support: If they use our Console, the quickest is to grab the Debug Token from the request details: Console -> Requests -> click the failing request -> copy "Debug token" and paste it here. That token lets us pull server-side traces without them attaching full logs.

ellie_c: I'll request the two requests + HAR + debug token and the curl example. Will share when they reply.

oncall_dg: If you paste the request id here I can jump into the trace and see where it hit the 502/504 :thumbsup:

ellie_c: Copying the example response headers they sent (sanitized):
`HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway`
`content-type: application/json`
`x-request-id: req_7a9b2f`
`x-trace-id: trace_20260316_1412`

ellie_c: attaching the failing request body and HAR in the ticket now. Thanks everyone!
